quote: So very bullish, um, a little bit trendy. I'm not the biggest fan of this sort of condition to be taking a reversals in, but it is, uh, a pretty nice extension. ... I mean this could like, you know, very easily lose and I'll just be happy with it. It's not the best condition.

quote: we were quite range bound now going into more of a bit more of an impulse So, you know, it's not the best condition ... I wouldn't say it's the best trade because it is quite directional and you don't really have the overextension on the 15 minute.
interpretation: Author took a UJ reversal while acknowledging an impulsive/directional condition and a missing 15m overextension; the loss is attributed (after the fact) to those two factors. Supports treating E1H-046 and 15m CB (E1H-021) as quality tiers rather than gates; outcome is not used for validity.

quote: um so this was kind of my initial take profit around here um most aggressive take profit is 50 of this extension
interpretation: In a trendy condition the 50%-of-extension target is described as the MOST AGGRESSIVE option, with a nearer initial TP. Consistent with E1H-038 (trendy -> target less than 50%) but conflicts with the unconditional wording of E1H-037 ('always targeting 50%').

quote: around 30 minutes just tends to be more consistent like more often than not I feel like you know around this sort of time you might have like some type of like shift or pullback but then you have around the 30 minute and it'll just like extend
interpretation: Shifts/pullbacks before :30 often fail because the :30 15m candle opens and extends further. Adds a mechanism for preferring :30+ over the :22 anchor in E1H-024.

quote: For like around 15 to 30 minutes in, like yeah they can be nice reversals but all All the time you can get like faked out as well. ... in general most of the time it's better off to be a little bit late than a little bit too early because then you can just get like stopped out before it goes in your favor
interpretation: Timing asymmetry: when unsure, enter later rather than earlier; 15-30 min reversals have more fake-outs. A tie-break for the :22/:37/:52 anchors.

quote: I guess what I kind of look for is like 22, 52, or 37 minutes into the hour. It's just like the XY correlation kind of helps with more specific timing. ... this is why i really like correlation for specific timing because like how do i know whether to enter here or here
interpretation: Correlation (DXY, yen basket) is used primarily to pick WHICH of the :22/:37/:52 anchors to act on (enter when the correlated instrument over-extends and then shifts). Sharpens E1H-044 from a direction check into a timing trigger.

quote: so might potentially enter around 38, 39 minutes into the hour. Dick's way just shifted bullish. potentially if we have gold spread shift bearish take out this low could be a decent sort of setup
interpretation: Gold entry trigger combines three shifts: DXY shifts opposite to the gold trade, the gold spread (XAU vs basket of non-USD currencies) shifts in the trade direction, and gold takes out the seconds low/high. Adds the gold spread as a second correlation instrument (not in existing records) and a conjunctive trigger.

quote: XAUEUR+XAUCAD+XAUGBP+XAUJPY+XAUAUD+XAUNZD+XAUXAG+XAUCHF • 1 • FOREX.com
interpretation: The 'gold spread' referred to in speech ('gold spreads', 'Goldsword', 'god spread') is a TradingView composite symbol summing gold priced in EUR, CAD, GBP, JPY, AUD, NZD, XAG and CHF on FOREX.com. Reproducible from public data. Composite formula read from OCR only.

quote: If you see the consolidation on gold, simply because we have gold spread and DXY both moving the same direction.
interpretation: When DXY and the gold spread move in the same direction, gold tends to consolidate; used as a reason not to enter. Complements E15-044 (gold and DXY same direction -> fake-out).

quote: Gold spread also shifted bullish. DXY is still bullish, not the biggest fan of that, but coming to some highs might be a reaction.
interpretation: Trade taken with DXY not yet confirming (still bullish on a gold buy) because DXY was into highs and the gold spread had shifted. DXY confirmation is not a gate.

quote: What I'm kind of waiting for, looking for, is a 5 minute, 15 minute candle to open, take out the previous high, or just create a top wick, push against me, and then potentially look for a setup to, like a shift, on the seconds time frame. I'm not the biggest fan of immediately pushing bearish off a 5 or 15 minute candle open,
interpretation: Extends E1H-021/E1H-022 in the hourly model to 5m candles as well: after a 5m or 15m open, wait for price to push against the trade (take the previous high/low or form the wick) before the seconds shift; avoid shifts created by the open itself pushing in the trade direction.

quote: I might close soon because we're approaching 52 minutes into the hour. ... Five minute candle opened, it immediately drove bearish Approaching 52 minutes into the hour so the halfway point of this five minute candle. It could definitely go down lower But there probably be a bit of a pullback before we go down lower. There is a chance though that this five minute candle could just Whip and push bullish
interpretation: Exit heuristic: near :52 (end of the reversal window), if a new 5m candle opens and drives strongly in the trade direction, close around that 5m candle's halfway point because it may wick back. The 5m analogue of E1H-033.

quote: When we're coming into around 2% on this previous move on some correlation, probably could have taken profit there after we took out this previous low as it was quite high volume, trendy. ... correlation was coming back into 50 of the previous move like around not exactly but around and we had some decrease in volume
interpretation: Exit signal (stated as a lesson): once price takes out the previous LTF low/high in your favour and the correlated instrument has retraced ~50% of its move with falling volume, take profit, especially in high-volume trendy conditions. Adds to E15-045 (DXY-based exit) and E1H-038.

quote: I just took profit after we took out this previous high around the open 50-minute candle. Ideally, you know, maybe we could have targeted 80% of this, but, you know, just felt like it, a bit of intuition.
interpretation: Manual TP after price takes out the previous high around the next 15m candle open (realised ~1.3R vs 1.6R tool). He also mentions targeting 80% in a range: a larger target variant not in E1H-038's wording. The close itself was intuition.

quote: I do the fifth hour of Asia because daylight savings you know the the second hour of Asia will change depending on when you're trading within the year for me it's like it can be either 11 a.m 12 p.m or even 1 p.m
interpretation: Session hours are counted relative to the Asia session, not local clock. Chart evidence pins the anchor: Fri 24 Oct 2025 15:38 UTC+11 = 'fifth hour of Asia' (V1H-trade_example_1), and 12:17-12:23 UTC+11 = 'second hour of Asia' (V1H-live_trade_2_uj_loss 00:00:02, V1H-live_trade_3_gold_win 00:00:04). Inference from three videos; confirm across more.

interpretation: MS alignment matters for continuations/direction trades, not for the small-reaction reversals he mainly trades. Downgrades E1H-045 for CBR reversals.

quote: when you're trading a trending range counter to the trending range um here you're always most likely to have a pullback a reaction after you take out a previous low in a bearish example
interpretation: Counter trending-range reversals are most likely right after the previous swing low (bearish TRR) / high (bullish TRR) is taken. Sharpens E1H-012 ('beyond structure') to 'immediately after taking out the previous swing'.

quote: So I'm trading counter direction, which is fine if it's more range bound, which it is.
interpretation: Counter-direction reversals are acceptable conditional on the MTF condition being range-bound. Implies they are less acceptable in trendier conditions (see CAND-001 for his practice).

quote: this is kind of more important if you're going for a bit bigger of a move if you're going for like low time frame scalps doesn't matter that much ... i'm just tracking that it's not the most important thing
interpretation: Daily CB (previous day close, first half of day push, relative to daily open) is tracked but only matters for bigger targets; irrelevant for LTF scalps. Consistent with E1H-028.
